summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 3.35/974)

data.turoyo: Xori ʕAziz: Haka eli mǧarabwayli, laxwa noše ḥrene lə mǧarable.
data.translation: Father Aziz: If I myself had tried it, otherwise no one else tried it.

rationale: New Preterit-wa box: explicit first-person L-agent with -wa. Short full clause preserves unresolved Haka/laxwa relation. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/48)

data.turoyo: Mǧarabbe ġắlăbe waxtən dʕəbri li+qriṯo. Mḥarabbe diḏan, lə+ṭralle ʕəbri.
data.translation: They tried many times to (re-)enter the village. Ours fought back, they did not let them (re-)enter.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: repeated attempts with finite d-complement.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Besim Martyrdom of Maferyono/15)

data.translation: He also tried once more, nothing happened to him.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: attempt and failed outcome in a short complete context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (61/147)

data.turoyo: Bi walayayo kula d əmmat ənsan fayəš rabo, naʕimo, faqiro, d l aṯi d lə mǧarable ruḥe bi xanǧar, lo fayəš. Bale lo qadiri d guršila w l aḏiʕi man yo, u sayomo d masalaṯe.
data.translation: Wenn du meinst, in der ganzen Stadt wäre ein Mensch übrig geblieben, gross oder klein, arm oder reich, der sich nicht an dem Dolche versucht hatte - keiner blieb übrig; aber sie konnten ihn nicht herausziehen, und man brachte den Täter dieser Sache nicht heraus. Zuhörer: Aber sie ist doch getan worden!

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: reflexive object with b-marked test object.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (107/29)

data.translation: Ich habe dich nur auf die Probe stellen wollen.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: overt personal suffix and cognate nominal material.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 15/80)

data.turoyo: ʕal naf diḏi kuraxno, mǧarbina ono w huwe ḥḏoḏe, <...>
data.translation: aber bei meiner Ehre, ich will gegen jenen ausziehen und wir, er und ich; wollen uns gegenseitig erproben. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: reciprocal test of opponents, retained under existing sense 1.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (36/137)

data.translation: Du willst mich wohl auf die Probe stellen?

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: personal testing with fronted cognate noun; also already illustrates the inherited Infinitiv cell.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (JTM 4.3/11)
rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: m-less ǧarəb, not evidence for a different stem.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (48/4)

data.turoyo: Hano məllele omər: "Mǧarabli! ʕAl šarṭ, d loweno, xəd kəbʕat, gxoṣanno u šarṭ."
data.translation: Jener sprach zu ihm: "Versuche es einmal mit mir, unter der Bedingung, daß ich, wenn ich nicht so bin, wie du wünschest, die Wette verliere."

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: personal suffix and explicit condition.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (61/171)

data.turoyo: Ya aḥunone, kobaʕno d adlalyo lo dəmxutu gab an nišaṯxu hul tloṯo lalye ǧarebunne w bəṯr!
data.translation: Brüder! Ihr dürft heute Nacht nicht bei euren Frauen schlafen; stellt sie erst drei Tage auf die Probe und dann!

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: plural m-less form with personal object suffix.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (115/176)

data.turoyo: U sayfayḏux hat, haka kəbʕət, d əḏʕət ze, mǧarab! Maḥat ʕəsri maǧidiye w mḥayene bu sayfayḏux!
data.translation: Dein Schwert, wenn du willst, versuch es doch! Lege zwanzig Taler aufeinander und schlage mit deinem Schwerte darauf!

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: practical test of a sword with its criterion stated.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (JTM 5.2/92)

data.turoyo: lə kuḏaʕno gərobo kəmǧarabli, lə kuḏaʕno. w msəkli haybe mene.
data.translation: Ich weiß nicht, ob er mich nur auf die Probe stellt, ich weiß es nicht. Er ist mir unheimlich.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infinitiv cell: g-spelled cognate noun before the testing verb, following inherited 36/137 allocation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.II/710)

data.turoyo: Bəṯər u ḥəlmayḏi d ʕubrono lu beṯ-ṣawbo yo. Mawxa ste mu zabnawo w hul l uʕdo, kəmǧarbono d maʕləyono i sohḏuṯayḏi.
data.translation: Then my dream is to enter university. So from that time until now I have been trying to raise my qualification.

rationale: Unusual feminine first-person Infectum kəmǧarbono with finite d-complement; adds person/gender coverage beyond the filled routine cell. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: versuchen, erproben, auf die Probe stellen; erfahren;
rationale: The inherited versuchen, erfahren under-specifies direct testing of a person, advice, medicine or horses, already implicit in the cognate-object example 36/137. Add erproben/auf die Probe stellen to make this established meaning explicit; do not split combat contexts into another sense.

summary: Attempts take finite d-clauses, reflexive ruḥo with b- or ʕal test domain, direct personal objects, or reciprocal ḥḏoḏe. Omitted complements are contextually recoverable. These frames support a broad try/test/experience sense.

The single inherited Preterit example is experiential; the new contexts also show deliberate attempts and personal tests. Infectum-wa describes repeated shooting practice. Arabic ǧrb II remains integrated as stem II, including m-less Imperativ ǧarəb / ǧarebunne.

Detransitive Part. Pass. mǧarbo-no (83/39) denotes the experienced participant, not simply someone undergoing a test. Cognate action nouns ǧerobo / gərobo follow the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv allocation despite agentive testing semantics.
The Preterit mǧarabbe in 61/167 already occurs within the inherited Imperativ example; its presence there is legitimate shared context, not a structure error requiring the example to be moved.
Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals remain prior material and are not re-proposed here.

Finite d-complements occur with human individual, collective and brain subjects. Testing with objects and deliberate attempts remain within the broad round-1 sense; no independently lexicalized collocation is established.
mǧarabwayli at 3.10/99 and 3.35/974 has a -wa Preterit base plus L-agent. The editorial restatement and interview wording are not counted as independent new senses or redundant examples.

The reader request to cross-index the initial Preterit within an existing Imperativ example does not identify a misfiled example: it also contains the actual Imperativ and round 1 already addressed this. No entry correction is repeated.
Provide correctly aligned edition translation for 111/102: the supplied alignment warning identifies material from the preceding verse. Neither occurrence is quoted as an addition.
In 93/58, what is the referent of mǧarbo, and does l ġalabe ruʕye belong to it or solely to the following clause? Is experiential proof conventional here?
Confirm segmentation and roles of mǧarabləx (PrS 75/77), Mǧarabnanne (36/108) and gəmǧarabna (30/21); retain exact source spelling and do not force morphology to match a free translation.
Is gərobo in JTM 5.2/92 certainly the cognate action noun, as suggested by the inherited 36/137 example?
Does practising an activity require iterative context, or is it a conventional use of mǧarəb? Existing JL 19.6/22 alone does not establish a separate lexical sense.

At Jan 3.35/974 and its editorial restatement 3.10/99, does Haka eli ... laxwa mean if I had tried, only I tried, or an unfinished conditional? Morphological Preterit-wa does not settle its discourse force.
Confirm contraction and feminine first-person segmentation of kəmǧarbono (Jan 4.II/710) without normalizing the printed form.
Testing applies to opponents (including reciprocal ḥḏoḏe), courtesy, advice, medicine and horses. The object can be ruḥo, a person, or an item under test; context supplies the test domain.
Detransitive Part. Pass. mǧarbo may predicate experiential validation of a belief in 93/58; this is provisional because its referent and relation to the following shepherd clause are unclear.
Repeated testing of shooting has a practice/training interpretation; the existing Infectum-wa example already contains it, so no new sense is needed.

Jan supports round-1 broad testing/attempt gloss: testing God and a person with riddles, attempting language use, educational improvement and social change. No separate experiment or test-person sense.
u meḥi as subject of kəmǧarəb d maləx is a participant extension to the brain in an explanatory psychology passage. No new sense of the verb.
